resources.string: Presses Skip on YouTube ads as soon as the button appears.
AutoSkip watches the YouTube app for the Skip button on ads and presses it for you. It only looks at YouTube, it does not collect or send anything, and it has no internet access.
Open YouTube and watch. The moment Skip appears, it\'s pressed.
Flip the switch below to start skipping again.
Turn it on once, and skippable YouTube ads get skipped for you.
What AutoSkip can and can\'t see
AutoSkip can\'t skip ads that have no Skip button, and it can\'t skip sooner than YouTube allows.
To press Skip for you, AutoSkip needs Android\'s Accessibility permission. Here is exactly what it does with it.
AutoSkip reads the YouTube app\'s screen, and only to find the Skip button. It does not look at your other apps.
AutoSkip has no internet permission, so Android itself stops it from sending anything anywhere. You can check this under App info, Permissions.
It taps the Skip button when YouTube shows it, and nothing else. Ads without a Skip button play as usual.

Next, Android will warn that AutoSkip can view and control your screen. Every app that uses Accessibility gets this same warning, whatever the app actually does. It is right to read it carefully. For AutoSkip, tap Allow.
Tap AutoSkip. It is under Installed apps or Downloaded apps.
If the switch is greyed out

Android blocks Accessibility for apps installed from a file until you allow it.

1. Tap Open App info below.
2. Tap the three dots at the top right.
3. Choose "Allow restricted settings".

Then come back and turn AutoSkip on.
